todayTheme: Is the evidence we use to judge agents reliable: eval oracles, boundary violations, and logs for change approval

candidates.title: When Agent Evaluation Becomes Unreliable: An Empirical Study of Oracle Failures and Configuration-Dependent Measurement in an LLM Agent Benchmark
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint, submitted to Empirical Software Engineering
candidates.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology
credibilityEvidence: Abstract + Sec 4.1: seven injected oracle defect classes all detected, repaired oracle no false positives
Sec 4.1: replay of recorded tool calls on clean DB, 4,194 -> 2,883 database passes over 4,320 episodes, success 94.3% -> 65.5%
Sec 1 contributions: explicitly no claim that the upstream runner inflates its own success rates
Sec 6 Threats to validity: no deterministic seed, RQ2/RQ3 bounded as measurement-process observations
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: One benchmark (tau-bench retail + airline) and a synthetic domain; port to a second benchmark failed on framework contract.
reproducibilityEvidence: Zenodo DOIs in paper; audit suite, fault catalogue, preregistration/deviation logs, frozen per-episode records, offline entry point
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Article only states the finding on a post-run scoring path and repeats the author disclaimer.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Single benchmark; method did not port to a second independently implemented benchmark.
candidates.presentationReason: Claims, scope and non-claims are stated explicitly.
candidates.reason: Strongest evidence of the day that a widely used agent benchmark scoring path can overstate success by ~29pp; complete offline replication package; anchors the evidence-reliability theme.

candidates.title: SWE-Misbehavior: Benchmarking and Mitigating Boundary Violations in Software Coding Agents
candidates.institution: National University of Singapore (WING) + A*STAR, UVA, Virginia Tech, Tufts
credibilityEvidence: Sec 4.1: OpenHands, smolagents, Agno, Claude Code x GPT-5 / Gemini-2.5-Flash / Qwen3-Coder-30B
Table 3: LLM judge vs 3 human annotators on 200 samples, Gemini-3-Flash avg 88.63% (IF 72.0%)
Findings 1-3 + abstract: dependency misread up to 98.5%, user-input modification 50.5%, env integrity 53%
Sec 5 + abstract: Code-KIT -52% (smolagents) / -32% (OpenHands) violations with improved completion
Limitations: no multi-turn security injection/exfiltration; Code-KIT per-step only
reproducibilityEvidence: GitHub repo with code and data
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Framework credible but model versions old; article hedges on transfer to frontier models.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Older models and short synthetic tasks.
candidates.presentationReason: HTML render drops many inline numbers; abstract and tables recoverable.
candidates.reason: Provides automatically measurable boundary-violation metrics for coding agents across 4 frameworks and shows tool-interface design drives violations; same problem class as same-day Copilot config-write CVE.

candidates.title: agent-risk: Risk Assessment for Changes to AI Agents
candidates.institution: University of Southern California (incl. law), London Business School, Arizona State University
communitySignals: GitHub yzhao062/agent-risk with code, registrations, logs
credibilityEvidence: Sec 3 Proposition 3.1: logging sufficiency for exact replay
Sec 4.1: 7,200-episode log decides neither retry gate; snapshot reruns match live (approve gate 2, decline gate 1); P(harm) frozen then matched within 0.015
Sec 4.1: reruns cost 15% of live calls for both gates, half of post-hoc-sized live test
Sec 4.4: new model reproduced 0 of 99 logged episodes
Limitations: one open-weight family (14B/27B), honest agents, bash sandbox + airline env
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Small controlled demonstrations on one model family.
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Article cites only sandbox demonstrations without extrapolation.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Model-release case unresolved; oversight-aware agents unbounded.
candidates.reason: Only candidate that addresses deployer-side evidence for approving agent changes from logs, matching today's regulatory evidence theme; formal results plus frozen-then-checked sandbox estimates.

candidates.title: The Agent Knew: Internal States Forecast Unauthorized Actions and Stop Them, and the Lies That Follow
candidates.reason: Abstract reports preregistered odds ratio 7.0 and residual-stream forecast AUROC 0.94, but requires white-box access to open-weight models, so its practical link for API-based deployers is weaker than agent-risk's log-design guidance; method section not yet read.

candidates.title: Which Metadata Matters for LLM Tool Selection in MCP? Evidence from Controlled Factor-Level Interventions
candidates.reason: Controlled single-factor interventions over 367,174 MCP tools are relevant to tool design, but the topic is tool selection rather than evidence reliability; SWE-Misbehavior covers the tool-interface angle with broader framework coverage today. Abstract-level only.

candidates.title: Re-executing Coding-Agent Evaluations: Unchanged Decisions and Unresolved Policy Risk
candidates.reason: Preregistered re-execution of SWE-bench Pro / DGM archive returns mostly negative results with a 4.95% upper limit; overlaps the oracle-audit paper's theme but reports weaker, inconclusive findings. Abstract-level only.

candidates.title: What Counts as the Same Task? Executable Contracts for Robustness Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents
candidates.reason: Embedding-threshold validity rules admitting 75-100% task-changing edits is a strong eval-validity finding, but narrower (robustness test construction) than the oracle-audit paper. Abstract-level only.

candidates.title: Judges Follow the Reference: The Derivation Gap in Verifying Tool-Call Arguments
candidates.reason: Derivation gap across seven tool-call judges is relevant to eval reliability; ranked below the oracle-audit paper because it measures judge bias rather than a concrete benchmark score distortion. Abstract-level only.

candidates.title: Audit tools of the trade: Automated Auditor Elicitation Can Be Sensitive to the Context the Auditor Is Given
candidates.reason: NeurIPS 2026 AIWILD workshop; Petri auditor context sensitivity on 1-10 scale is useful but effect sizes are small and limited to four auditor-target pairs. Abstract-level only.

candidates.title: Instructions Are Evidence, Not Objectives: Measuring Outcome Alignment of Agents
candidates.reason: SWE-chat analysis (56% of instructions omit later-needed requirements) is interesting but about requirement inference, off today's evidence-reliability theme. Abstract-level only.

candidates.title: CWE-bench: Refocusing Agentic Security from Exploitation to Defense
candidates.reason: Private 120-task defensive benchmark; private held-out set limits reproducibility compared with selected papers' full artifacts. Abstract-level only.

candidates.title: Revocation Is Not Complete at Receipt: An Executable Outcome Contract for Distributed Agent-Tool Gateways
candidates.reason: Gateway revocation contract with 14-case fault matrix is relevant to governance, but evaluation is a derived audit of eight cases, thinner than agent-risk. Abstract-level only.
